Subject: Dedicated sizing guidance for inference (H100/A100/L4)

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our infra team pushed a rough traffic surface for our clinical summarization APIs and we need a vendor-backed recommendation on SKU mix and memory profiles for a Dedicated cluster. High level:
- P95 latency budget (end-to-end) for real-time requests: 120ms
- Typical sequence lengths: 512 tokens (inference average), with occasional 2k for long summaries
- Concurrent active sessions: ~120 qps peak for realtime route, plus batch jobs overnight

We're sensitive to both unit cost and risk of OOMs for the occasional long requests. Can you advise on trade-offs between H100(80GB), A100(40GB), and L4(48GB) for this workload? Also interested in a fallback strategy if H100 capacity is constrained on Dedicated.

If helpful, I can share a sample payload set and cost target range. Looking to finalize procurement guidance by next Tuesday.

Hi Ava — thanks for the detail and the quick turnaround. Attaching a short modeling spreadsheet (mem_vs_latency_modeling.xlsx) with three scenario profiles: latency-optimized, cost-optimized, and mixed. High level takeaways up front:

- H100 (80GB): best headroom for long sequences and high-QPS sustained KV cache; lowest per-token latency at high batch sizes but highest monthly reserved cost. Strongly recommended where you expect many 2k+ sequences and want a single model variant without partitioning.

- A100 (40GB): good middle ground. Requires model/route sharding for very long sequences (split or dynamic offload), but much lower commitment cost. If you can limit peak async/batch to overnight for very long jobs, A100 is a solid cost-latency trade.

- L4 (48GB, tensor cores for int8/4-bit): best for cheap realtime low-latency lightweight routes and as a fallthrough for degraded quality non-critical requests. Works well with aggressive quantization and prefix-caching. Not recommended as sole option for 2k sequences unless you accept higher inference steps and quality tuning.

Recommended approach for Cerebrum (proposal):
1) Primary pool: mix of H100 (30%) + A100 (50%) to cover long tails and steady throughput. H100s reserved to support 2k sequences and high KV working sets.
2) Realtime burst/fallthrough: L4 pool (20%) for sub-128 token low latency routes and cost-sensitive degraded-mode where slight quality delta is acceptable.
3) Canary & rollout: start with a 2-instance H100 pilot on your Dedicated environment for the model and KV cache warmup; measure prefix-cache hit-rate before scaling to full commit.

I've attached mem_vs_latency_modeling.xlsx with assumptions (batching curves, kv-cache hit-rate sensitivity, quantization impact) and a draft MAAP (mutual action plan) doc (maap_plan_v1.docx) that lays out milestones.

Next steps: Would you like us to run a quick benchmark with your sample payload (we can do a 2-day run on our hosted infra and provide masking) or prepare a committed cost estimate for 6/12/24 month reserved mixes?

Cheers,
Stephanie Nguyen

Ava / Stephanie — quick technical notes to complement the modeling sheet:

- Memory working set: for 2k sequences you need a sustained KV cache and model activation headroom. H100 80GB avoids activation chopping for most larger families; A100 40GB will require KV sharding or offload for >1.2M KV entries per shard.
- Latency: P95 token generation improves with continuous batching but hurts tail for realtime single-token interactions. For your 120 qps target, aim for dynamic batching windows of ~10-25ms to keep p95 under 120ms while benefiting from batching.
- Quantization: L4 is excellent with int8/4-bit profiles for the smaller prompts. Recommend keeping two quantized variants in the catalog: q8_128 (fast low-memory) and q4_512 (aggressive cost saver, for batch only).
- Fallback logic: route policy we recommend:
  1) Try primary (H100/A100) with cached KV prefix
  2) If queue depth > 150ms or model cold start, route to L4 quantized variant with degraded scoring threshold
  3) If request indicates >1500 tokens, convert to async batch (return 202 + callback)

I'll also add notes to the modeling sheet about the assumed kernel-level perf on H100 for flash attention variants vs A100. Happy to run a quick stress run if you provide sample traces.

— Dev
